pr_chain.title: Fix nullable enum deserialization in Kotlin OpenAPI generator
pr_chain.description:
When generating Kotlin enum classes from OpenAPI specifications, enums marked as `nullable: true` are not handled correctly. The `fromValue` companion function currently returns a non-nullable enum type even when the enum can be null, and it doesn't handle the case where null values should be gracefully accepted rather than throwing an exception.

    The issue is in the `kotlinEnumClass.mustache` template used by the OpenAPI generator. For nullable enums, the generated code should:
    1. Return a nullable enum type (`EnumType?`) from the `fromValue` function
    2. Not throw `IllegalArgumentException` when the value doesn't match any enum constant (it should return null instead)

    This is causing runtime failures when null values are encountered in API responses or when deserializing JSON payloads with null enum fields.

    The goal is to update the template so that nullable enums generate correct Kotlin code that compiles and behaves properly. We also need to add test coverage to verify that nullable enums are generated correctly.

## Environment Setup
Check the following files for build and test setup:
    - `openapi/openapi-generator/build.gradle` - module-specific build configuration
    - `build.gradle` - root build configuration
    - `settings.gradle` - project structure
    - `gradle.properties` - Gradle properties
    - `dependencies.gradle` - dependency management
    The repository uses Gradle; use `gradlew` wrapper for all build commands.

## Implementation Plan
1. Locate the `kotlinEnumClass.mustache` template file at `openapi/openapi-generator/src/main/resources/openapi/templates/kora/kotlinEnumClass.mustache`.
    2. Modify the `fromValue` function signature in the companion object to include the nullable modifier `?` on the return type when `isNullable` is true.
    3. Update the function body so that the `throw IllegalArgumentException` is only generated for non-nullable enums (it should already be conditioned on `{{^isNullable}}`).
    4. Create a new test OpenAPI specification at `openapi/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/example/petstoreV3_enum.yaml` that includes:
       - A nullable enum field (`nullable: true`)
       - A non-nullable required enum field
       - A non-required, non-nullable enum field
       - An enum field with `nullable: false` explicitly set
    5. Add the new test specification to the test file collection in `KoraCodegenTest.java` to ensure it runs through all generation modes.
    6. Verify that the generated Kotlin code compiles successfully in all Kotlin modes (KOTLIN_CLIENT, KOTLIN_SUSPEND_CLIENT, KOTLIN_SERVER, KOTLIN_SUSPEND_SERVER).

pr_chain.title: Fix equals & hashCode for fieldless Kotlin OpenAPI models
pr_chain.description:
In the Kora OpenAPI Generator, Kotlin model classes that declare no fields (i.e., empty classes without any properties) are currently generated as plain classes without an `equals` or `hashCode` implementation. This violates the expected equals/hashCode contract for such models and can cause incorrect behavior when instances are used in collections or compared.

    Update the Mustache template used to generate Kotlin models so that when a model has no variables (`hasVars` is false), the generated class includes explicit `equals` and `hashCode` methods. The `equals` method should check reference equality first (`this === other`), then verify the class types match (`javaClass == other?.javaClass`), and return `true` if both checks pass. The `hashCode` method should return the hash code of the class (`javaClass.hashCode()`).

    Ensure that this behavior is only applied to models without fields — models with fields should continue to be generated as Kotlin `data class`es (which already provide correct `equals`/`hashCode` implementations).

## Environment Setup
Review the repository's build configuration to understand how to install dependencies and run tests. The relevant files include:
    - `build.gradle` (root project build script)
    - `settings.gradle` (project/module declarations)
    - `gradle.properties` (project properties)
    - `dependencies.gradle` (dependency versions)
    - `gradle/ci-tests.gradle`, `gradle/in-test-generated.gradle`, `gradle/kotlin-plugin.gradle` (build/test helpers)
    - The module-specific build file `openapi/openapi-generator/build.gradle`

    The repo uses Gradle (with the Gradle wrapper `gradlew` at the root). Check the `README.md` for any additional project-specific setup instructions.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open the template file `openapi/openapi-generator/src/main/resources/openapi/templates/kora/kotlinModel.mustache`.
    2. Locate the section of the template that renders the class body for non-enum, non-discriminator models (the block following the class declaration and constructor).
    3. Add a Mustache section guarded by `{{^hasVars}}` that emits the following methods inside the class body:
       - An `override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean` method that:
         - Returns `true` if `this === other`.
         - Returns `false` if `other` is null or of a different class (`javaClass != other?.javaClass`).
         - Otherwise returns `true`.
       - An `override fun hashCode(): Int` method that returns `javaClass.hashCode()`.
    4. Place this block in a location where it is rendered inside the class body for any model that has no fields. Verify that the surrounding Mustache tags properly open/close the block so it only appears when `hasVars` is false.
    5. Ensure the change does not affect models with fields — those should still be rendered as `data class` and not include the explicit methods.

pr_chain.title: Fix @Retry aspect to properly handle CompletableFuture return types
pr_chain.description:
We need to fix the `@Retry` annotation processing for methods that return `CompletableFuture`. Currently, the `RetryKoraAspect` generates code that always expects a `CompletionStage` return type from the retry mechanism, but when the method returns a `CompletableFuture` specifically, the generated code produces a type mismatch — the `retry()` call returns a `CompletionStage` which cannot be directly returned as a `CompletableFuture`.

    The goal is to update the aspect so that when the annotated method's return type is exactly `CompletableFuture`, the generated retry expression is converted using `.toCompletableFuture()` to match the expected return type. Methods returning `CompletionStage` should continue to work as before.

    Additionally, we should add test coverage to verify that `@Retry`, as well as other resilient annotations (`@CircuitBreaker`, `@Fallback`, `@Timeout`), work correctly with both `CompletionStage` and `CompletableFuture` return types.

## Environment Setup
The developer should check the following repo files for build and test setup:
    - `build.gradle` (root) for overall build configuration
    - `settings.gradle` for module listing
    - `resilient/resilient-annotation-processor/build.gradle` for module-specific dependencies and test configuration
    - `gradle/ci-tests.gradle` for test-related Gradle configuration
    - `.github/workflows/test-pr.yml` for CI test pipeline

## Implementation Plan
1. Inspect the `RetryKoraAspect.java` file in `resilient/resilient-annotation-processor/src/main/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/resilient/annotation/processor/aop/`
    2. In the `buildBodyFuture` method, check the return type of the annotated method using `method.getReturnType()`
    3. If the return type is exactly `java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture`, append `.toCompletableFuture()` to the generated retry expression
    4. Update the test data classes in `resilient/resilient-annotation-processor/src/test/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/resilient/annotation/processor/aop/testdata/` to include both `CompletionStage` and `CompletableFuture` variants for each resilient annotation target
    5. Add or update test classes to verify both return type variants work for retry, circuit breaker, fallback, and timeout annotations

pr_chain.title: Improve HTTP server/client logging messages and console log format alignment
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to enhance the readability and consistency of log output across HTTP client and server telemetry, as well as the console text record encoder. Specifically:

    1. Update the HTTP client logger (`Sl4fjHttpClientLogger`) so log messages are prefixed with "HttpClient" for both requests and responses (e.g., "HttpClient requesting …", "HttpClient received …"). Also change the message for a missing response to "HttpClient received No HttpResponse from …".
    2. Update the HTTP server logger (`Slf4jHttpServerLogger`) so log messages are prefixed with "HttpServer" (e.g., "HttpServer received request for …", "HttpServer responded …"). For error responses, include the exception message inline (e.g., "HttpServer responded error 500 for … due to: <message>") when stacktrace logging is disabled. When statusCode is null and there is no exception, log at INFO level with message "HttpServer responded for …".
    3. Refactor `DefaultHttpClientTelemetry` so that the `operation` string is only computed when a logger is present and either request or response logging is enabled. This means the `TelemetryContextData` record constructor should accept the operation as a parameter rather than computing it internally.
    4. Update the `ConsoleTextRecordEncoder` so the log level is printed immediately after the timestamp, before the thread name, with appropriate padding to align levels of different lengths. Also change the separator between the logger name and the message from a single space to " - ".
    5. Adjust `LogAspect` in the declarative-logging annotation processor so that generated code uses `addStatement` instead of a bare `add` call for `gen.writeFieldName(...)`.
    6. Update the existing `DefaultHttpClientTelemetryTest` so that mocked `HttpClientLogger` instances also stub `logResponse()` to return `true` (needed after the telemetry changes).

    Ensure all existing tests in the affected modules still pass.

## Environment Setup
Check the repository root `build.gradle`, `settings.gradle`, and `dependencies.gradle` for build configuration. Each module has its own `build.gradle`; relevant modules for this task include `http/http-client-common/build.gradle`, `http/http-server-common/build.gradle`, `logging/logging-logback/build.gradle`, and `logging/declarative-logging/declarative-logging-annotation-processor/build.gradle`. The `gradlew` script is the Gradle wrapper. Look for test configuration in these files to understand how to run tests.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify `http/http-client-common/src/main/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/http/client/common/telemetry/Sl4fjHttpClientLogger.java`: prefix request/response log messages with "HttpClient", adjust the "no response" message.
    - Modify `http/http-server-common/src/main/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/http/server/common/telemetry/Slf4jHttpServerLogger.java`: prefix all messages with "HttpServer", add exception message in non-stacktrace error paths, use INFO for null status with no exception.
    - Modify `http/http-client-common/src/main/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/http/client/common/telemetry/DefaultHttpClientTelemetry.java`: change `TelemetryContextData` constructor to accept operation; compute operation only when logger exists and logging is active.
    - Modify `logging/logging-logback/src/main/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/logging/logback/ConsoleTextRecordEncoder.java`: reorder log level to appear right after timestamp with padding, change logger-message separator to " - ".
    - Modify `logging/declarative-logging/declarative-logging-annotation-processor/src/main/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/logging/aspect/LogAspect.java`: replace `b.add("gen.writeFieldName($S);", ...)` with `b.addStatement(...)`.
    - Update `http/http-client-common/src/test/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/http/client/common/telemetry/DefaultHttpClientTelemetryTest.java` to stub `logResponse()` returning `true` in the two logging tests.

We need to improve the error messages that get thrown when a method annotated with @Cacheable or @CacheInvalidate doesn't have the right number of arguments for the cache key. Right now the message is confusing — let's make it explicitly say it expects at least one cache key method argument when there are none, and also clarify the wording for the upper limit so it reads as "method arguments" instead of just "parameters". Please update both the annotation processor and the symbol processor so the behavior is consistent.

pr_chain.title: Fix Wrapped component injection and add mockComponent with dependency removal in Kora JUnit5 extension
pr_chain.description:
Fix `@TestComponent` injection support for components that are wrapped in `Wrapped` (e.g., `LifecycleWrapper`). When a test requests injection of a bean whose actual graph node type is `Wrapped<T>`, the extension must unwrap the `Wrapped` value and inject the underlying instance.

    Additionally, add a new `mockComponent` method to `KoraGraphModification` that replaces a graph node with a mock supplier AND removes dependencies of the original component (unlike `replaceComponent`, which keeps the original dependencies). This is useful for Mockito-based tests where the mock should not have its real dependencies wired.

    Ensure the following works:
    - Injection of field and method parameter types that are wrapped in `Wrapped` — both when the requested type matches the wrapped value type and when it matches via assignability.
    - Injection of types that are wrapped in custom implementations of `Wrapped` (not just `LifecycleWrapper`).
    - `mockComponent` works with and without tags.
    - Existing `replaceComponent` behavior is preserved (keeps dependencies).

## Environment Setup
Check `test/test-junit5/build.gradle` and the root `build.gradle` for module dependencies and test configuration. For the overall build and test runner, inspect the root `settings.gradle`, `gradle.properties`, `dependencies.gradle`, and the Gradle wrapper scripts (`gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`). CI test configuration hints can be found in `.github/workflows/test-pr.yml` and `.github/workflows/test-master.yml`.

## Implementation Plan
- Modify `GraphUtils` node-lookup methods to detect graph node types that implement `Wrapped` and match against the wrapped value type (not the wrapper type) when searching by type or assignable type.
    - Modify `KoraJUnit5Extension`'s component resolution logic (both for `Class` and `ParameterizedType` candidates) to unwrap objects that are `Wrapped` instances and match the wrapped value against the requested type and tags.
    - Add a new record `GraphReplacementNoDeps` (or equivalent) that replaces a node without preserving that node's dependencies; `replaceNode` should be invoked with a function that does not provide access to the original dependencies.
    - Rename the existing `GraphReplacement` to `GraphReplacementWithDeps` and update `KoraGraphModification.replaceComponent` methods to use it, maintaining current behavior.
    - Add overloaded `mockComponent(Type, Supplier)` and `mockComponent(Type, List<Class<?>>, Supplier)` methods to `KoraGraphModification` that add `GraphReplacementNoDeps` modifications.
    - Add test coverage: new test classes for wrapped injection (`InjectWrapperTests`) and mock component with dependency removal (`MockGraphModificationMockTests`), and update test data in `TestApplication` to include wrapped components.

pr_chain.title: Extend Kora OpenAPI generator to support URI, duration, and time format types
pr_chain.description:
The goal is to extend the Kora OpenAPI generator so that it properly maps additional OpenAPI string format types to their corresponding Java types. Currently, the generator only maps `date`, `DateTime`, `UUID`, and `BigDecimal` formats. We need to add support for `time`, `duration`, and `uri` formats, mapping them to `java.time.OffsetTime`, `java.time.Duration`, and `java.net.URI` respectively.

    Additionally, we need to ensure that the generated code compiles correctly across all supported modes (Java and Kotlin, client and server variants). To verify this, we must add a new test resource YAML file that exercises these new type mappings, and register this new test resource in the existing parameterized test suite so it runs against all generator modes.

    The implementation should be minimal and focused - just extend the existing type mapping and add a test case. No broader refactoring or restructuring is needed.

## Environment Setup
This is a Gradle project. Check `build.gradle` at the repository root, `openapi/openapi-generator/build.gradle`, and `dependencies.gradle` to understand the build structure and dependencies. The root `settings.gradle` includes all modules. The `gradle/ci-tests.gradle` file may contain test configuration. Tests for the OpenAPI generator live in `openapi/openapi-generator/src/test/`.

## Implementation Plan
- Locate the `KoraCodegen.java` file in `openapi/openapi-generator/src/main/java/ru/tinkoff/kora/openapi/generator/`.
    - In the `typeMapping` map, add entries for `time`, `duration`, and `uri` formats, mapping them to `java.time.OffsetTime`, `java.time.Duration`, and `java.net.URI` respectively. Ensure the `importMapping` already includes `URI` and `OffsetTime` (add `Duration` if missing).
    - Create a new OpenAPI YAML test resource file (e.g., `petstoreV3_types.yaml`) in `openapi/openapi-generator/src/test/resources/example/` that exercises these new type formats across a schema.
    - In `KoraCodegenTest.java`, add the new YAML file to the `files` array in the `generateParams()` method so it gets tested against all supported generator modes.
    - Run the existing test suite for the OpenAPI generator module to verify the new types generate and compile correctly in all modes, fixing any issues that arise.
